frameworks.reason: Ada’s obligations pull in different directions. She has promised Cara the medicine, while helping Ben offers a much greater chance of saving a life. The deontological agent treats keeping a promise as a strict duty and helping others as a duty that leaves some discretion about how to act. It records a preference for Cara. Yet the saved duty assessment marks both choices as conflicted: treating Ben breaks the promise, while treating Cara raises the competing demand to help Ben. The record does not establish that the promise overrides the rescue obligation in this emergency.
